answers.answer: In a 3-player Census the tied leaders gain nothing, and the unique last player pays 1 coin. In an unequal 2-player Census, the unique leader gains 1 coin, but the last player never pays.
answers.evidence: Census: “tied lead gives no coin”; “unique last player pays 1 coin”; “In a 2-player game the last player never pays”

answers.answer: No. Draw up to the allowance of 6, limited by free Market spaces, so you may draw at most 2. Undrawn Market Followers remain between rounds and occupy capacity.
answers.evidence: Followers: “up to the allowance… limited by free Market spaces”; “Unused Market Followers remain… and occupy capacity”

answers.answer: You may fill an action gradually over multiple rounds, but it activates only when all required spaces are occupied by Followers or legal Technology (Town Hall needs only one of its two spaces). You may save a fully activated action for a later round. When an ordinary action is executed, its Followers return to your bag; Technology stays on its spaces.
answers.evidence: Planning: “fill an action gradually over multiple rounds”; “activation can be saved”; Actions: ordinary action Followers return to bag; Technology stays

answers.answer: Starting with Start Player, players act clockwise repeatedly, taking one activated action or passing per turn. Passing is final for you that Action Phase, even with unused activations. Unused activations keep their Followers on the board for future rounds.
answers.evidence: Actions: “one activated action or passing”; “Passing ends your participation”; “Unused activations… keep their Followers on the board”

answers.answer: Farm House requires Boatman + Craftsman; it puts a new Farmer in your bag, advances the Farmers Track one space, and gives the good depicted at that space.
answers.evidence: Actions table: Farm House effect

answers.answer: Village lets you recruit one Boatman, Craftsman, or Trader, put it in your bag, and advance that profession’s track one space. Boatman: gain depicted coins, except first to last space gets a Citizen instead. Craftsman: gain a Technology tile, usable only after you pass. Trader: gain one Place Tile; first advance allows category I only, later advances I or II.
answers.evidence: Village recruitment bullets

answers.answer: The newly recruited Craftsman’s Technology cannot help another action this Action Phase: it is used only after you pass. Your first Technology must replace a Farmer. A Technology cannot move once placed; later Technologies can replace any profession except Monk; at most one per Place, none at a Place requiring only one Follower. Technology remains on its space after execution.
answers.evidence: Technology placement limits; Village recruitment: “use it only after you pass”

answers.answer: No. The first Trader-track advance permits category I only; every later advance allows category I or II. Players may inspect the Place Tile stacks at any time.
answers.evidence: Village recruitment Trader; Setup: “Players may inspect these stacks at any time”

answers.answer: University requires Farmer + Craftsman + Trader, recruits a Scholar into your bag, advances Scholars Track one space, and gives its depicted Development Points. Castle requires Farmer + Boatman + Trader, recruits a Knight into your bag, and advances Knights Track; the fourth Knight leaves allowance at 7, with the first player there taking its Citizen. Monastery requires Scholar + Trader, recruits a Monk into your bag with no extra track reward. Once a character track is at its last space, that action cannot be taken again.
answers.evidence: Actions table; Castle rewards; Character-track limits

answers.answer: Yes. On ordinary actions, a Monk may replace any other profession, including Knight. A Knight or Technology cannot replace a required Monk. Monks (and other substitutions) cannot replace the exact professions depicted on Beneficial Deeds.
answers.evidence: Monks: “Monk can replace any other profession. The reverse is forbidden”; Town Hall: substitutions cannot replace exact Deed professions

answers.answer: One Ship moves your Merchant along one adjacent Waterway (blue connection); one Wagon moves along one adjacent Road (brown connection). You may take at most one good from that connection, choosing one if several are there; taking it is optional. Empty connections are legal and give no good.
answers.evidence: Movement and goods paragraph

answers.answer: Guildhall builds one Trading Station in the town where your Merchant currently is. A town with any player’s station cannot receive another, except Orléans, where each player may build one station.
answers.evidence: Building paragraph

answers.answer: Scriptorium gives 1 Development Point by moving one space on the Development Track. Moving onto or past a coin space collects its depicted coins; the first player onto/past a Citizen space collects that Citizen; reaching/passing a Development Status space immediately changes your Status to its shown value.
answers.evidence: Actions table: Scriptorium; Scoring: Development Point effects

answers.answer: Town Hall works with one or two neutral Followers of any profession; one is enough, and one or both may be sent in a single action. Starting marked Followers cannot enter it. Send each permanently to a free Beneficial Deed space matching its exact profession, possibly on different Deeds. Take each space’s depicted 1, 2, or 3 coins; at Canalization choose 1 coin or 1 Development Point. Whoever fills a Deed’s last space takes its Citizen.
answers.evidence: Town Hall and Beneficial Deeds paragraph

answers.answer: Pilgrimage forbids Monk recruitment in that round’s Action Phase, before Phase 6. Other events resolve in Phase 6 after Actions. The setup puts the lighter Pilgrimage tile on top, so it opens round 1.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure phases 1 and 6; Setup: Pilgrimage on top

answers.answer: Only grain, cheese, or wine qualify as food; wool does not. Paid food goes to the Goods Market. If you have no food, you owe 5 coins; if you have fewer than five, you pay available coins and undergo torture for each missing coin.
answers.evidence: Harvest event; Torture: “pay available coins… each missing coin”

answers.answer: The neutral Scholar is lost from your bag and returns to its game-board supply, becoming recruitable again; its track marker does not move back. If Plague draws your marked starting Trader, you keep it and lose no Follower that round; no replacement draw is made.
answers.evidence: Plague event

answers.answer: Pay the one coin you have, then cover the two missing coins with any mix of eligible items: a built or unbuilt Trading Station; one random eligible neutral Follower drawn only from your bag (return and redraw marked starters until neutral); one Development Point per missing coin by moving left, never onto or past a coin space; or a Goods, Place, or Technology tile. Items surrendered are removed from the game. Market or Action Space Followers cannot be used; marked starters cannot be lost.
answers.evidence: Torture (bankruptcy) paragraph

answers.answer: You cannot play an action that provides an unavailable Character, Technology, or Goods tile, even if another part would give a reward. It becomes available again when the required tile is back in stock, subject to normal requirements. If the common coin supply is insufficient, players cannot receive coins at that moment.
answers.evidence: Limited supplies paragraph

answers.answer: A tie for most built Trading Stations gives the bonus Citizen to nobody. Final goods values are grain 1, cheese 2, wine 3, wool 4, brocade 5 points each. Stations and collected Citizens score (built stations + Citizens) × final Development Status. Equal scores go to the player furthest ahead on the Development Track; if still tied, share victory.
answers.evidence: Scoring/Victory Conditions; goods table

answers.answer: Each player receives a board, bag, Merchant, 10 Trading Stations, 5 coins, 7 markers, and four marked starting Followers. Put the four Followers on your Market, Merchant in Orléans, one marker on the first space of each of six Character Tracks and the Development Track, and keep coins and unbuilt stations in front of you. The youngest player takes the Start Player token.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 2 and youngest player

answers.answer: Put 13 Citizens on their marked board/Deed spaces and set the remaining Citizen aside for the final Trading Station award. Sort neutral Followers by profession into their buildings; set Technology in its supply. Separate Place Tiles into category I and II stacks, inspectable at any time. In a 4-player game shuffle goods face down and deal one face up onto every eligible Road/Waterway goods space; put remaining goods face up in the Goods Market.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 1, 3, 5

answers.answer: For 3 players remove 2 neutral Farmers, Boatmen, Craftsmen, and Traders each; 3 neutral Knights, Scholars, and Monks each; 6 random goods; leave spaces marked 4 empty. For 2 players remove 4 of each Farmer/Boatman/Craftsman/Trader; 6 of each Knight/Scholar/Monk; 12 random goods; leave spaces marked 3 or 4 empty. Remove all starting Followers of unused colors.
answers.evidence: Fewer players table; “Remove all starting Followers of unused colors”

answers.answer: Farm House: Boatman + Craftsman. Village: Farmer + Boatman + Craftsman. University: Farmer + Craftsman + Trader. Castle: Farmer + Boatman + Trader. Monastery: Scholar + Trader.
answers.evidence: Actions table: required Followers

answers.answer: Ship: Farmer + Boatman + Knight. Wagon: Farmer + Trader + Knight. Guildhall: Farmer + Craftsman + Knight.
answers.evidence: Actions table: required Followers

answers.answer: Scriptorium requires Knight + Scholar. Town Hall allows any one or two neutral Followers; starting marked Followers are excluded from Town Hall.
answers.evidence: Actions table; Town Hall and Beneficial Deeds

answers.answer: Yes. For each of two declined draws, you may instead move one assigned Follower from an Action Space back to your Market. You cannot move a Follower directly from one Action Space to another.
answers.evidence: Followers phase: “For each draw you decline…”

answers.answer: Yes, you may inspect your bag at any time, but shuffle its contents afterward.
answers.evidence: Followers phase

answers.answer: The seven phases are Hour Glass, Census, Followers, Planning, Actions, Event, Start Player. Pass the Start Player token to the player on your left. Plan simultaneously and announce completion; if order matters, plan clockwise from Start Player. Payments and necessary order-sensitive event resolution are clockwise from Start Player. Paid coins go to common supply; received coins come from it.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure phases 1–7

answers.answer: Do not score immediately. Finish the entire round in which the 18th Hour Glass tile is drawn, including that round’s event; scoring follows.
answers.evidence: Scoring: “Finish the entire round… including its event”

answers.answer: The uniquely ahead player on the Farmers Track gains 1 coin; Census compares track markers regardless of how many Farmer tiles are in bags.
answers.evidence: Census paragraph

answers.answer: Income pays coins equal to your current Development Status.
answers.evidence: Income event; Status determines Income

answers.answer: Eight goods mean 2 coins (one per complete group of 3, rounded down). Goods types do not affect the count. A shortfall causes torture.
answers.evidence: Taxes: count all goods; pay 1 coin per complete group of 3, round down; shortfall causes torture

answers.answer: You receive 4 coins: Trading Day pays 1 per built Trading Station; unbuilt reserve stations do not count.
answers.evidence: Trading Day event; scoring distinguishes built stations

answers.answer: Hayrick: Farmer; take 1 grain from Goods Market. Cheese Factory: Farmer + Farmer; take 1 cheese from Goods Market. Winery: Farmer + Trader; take 1 wine from Goods Market. Wool Manufacturer: Boatman + Trader; take 1 wool from Goods Market. Tailor Shop: Scholar + Trader; take 1 brocade from Goods Market. Each goods-producing Place cannot be used when that particular good is absent from the Goods Market.
answers.evidence: 20 base Place Tiles table; goods-producing Place rule

answers.answer: Shipping Line: Boatman; gain 1 Development Point. Brewery: Monk; gain 2 coins. Windmill: Craftsman + Craftsman; gain 2 coins and 1 Development Point. Library: Knight + Scholar; gain 2 Development Points.
answers.evidence: 20 base Place Tiles table

answers.answer: Any one Follower activates Pharmacy. Pay 1–3 coins, advancing one Development space per coin; paying 2 advances two spaces. Zero and four coins are not legal.
answers.evidence: Pharmacy table: any 1 Follower; pay 1–3, one space per coin, at least 1 and no more than 3

answers.answer: Cellar: Monk + Scholar, gain 4 coins. Office: Scholar + Scholar, gain 1 coin per built Trading Station you have. Hospital: Boatman + Scholar, gain coins equal to current Development Status.
answers.evidence: 20 base Place Tiles table

answers.answer: Horse Wagon requires Trader + Knight; move along one Road to an adjacent town and collect one good if available.
answers.evidence: 20 base Place Tiles table

answers.answer: Laboratory requires Scholar + Craftsman and gives a Technology tile, subject to normal Technology placement limits. Your first Technology cannot be placed there because it must replace a Farmer. A later Technology may go on either Laboratory space if none is already there and usual constraints are met.
answers.evidence: 20 base Place Tiles table: Laboratory

answers.answer: Bathhouse requires Farmer. Draw 3 Followers from your bag, choose 2, and immediately place them on appropriate Action Spaces; none may go on Bathhouse. Return the third drawn Follower and the activating Bathhouse Follower to your bag.
answers.evidence: Bathhouse table

answers.answer: Place the one legally placeable drawn Follower on an appropriate Action Space other than Bathhouse. Return the other two drawn Followers and activating Bathhouse Follower to your bag. If none can be placed, place none and return all three drawn Followers plus the activating Follower to your bag.
answers.evidence: Bathhouse: “If you can legally place only one or none…”

answers.answer: It need not wait: a Place completed during this Action Phase is available on a later one of your action turns in the same phase, as long as you have not passed.
answers.evidence: Actions: Place completed during Action Phase available on a later action turn

answers.answer: Sacristy requires Monk. If activated, during Phase 6 return its Monk to your bag instead of suffering a negative event such as Harvest, Taxes, or Plague.
answers.evidence: Sacristy table

answers.answer: No. Pilgrimage prohibits Monk recruitment during Phase 5 Actions. Sacristy’s protection is applied in Phase 6, so it does not permit Monk recruitment during that earlier phase.
answers.evidence: Hour Glass phase: Pilgrimage prohibits Monk recruitment during Phase 5; Sacristy protection in Phase 6

answers.answer: Herb Garden lets Boatmen replace Craftsmen, Traders, and Farmers on ordinary actions. It does not permit replacement of Knights, Scholars, or Monks.
answers.evidence: Herb Garden table

answers.answer: School lets Scholars replace other professions except Monks on ordinary actions. It requires no activation. A Scholar cannot replace a required Monk.
answers.evidence: School table

answers.answer: No. Beneficial Deed spaces require exact professions; substitutions, including Herb Garden or School abilities, cannot replace the exact Deed types. Gunpowder Tower’s Deed option has the same exact-type requirement, so it does not change this.
answers.evidence: Town Hall: substitutions cannot replace exact Deed professions; Gunpowder Tower table: Deed spaces still require exact types

answers.answer: Gunpowder Tower adds 2 Market spaces. During Phase 3 place 1 or 2 drawn Followers there. In Planning move one or both to Action Spaces; alternatively, during Actions send one or both directly to Beneficial Deeds in a single action. Starting marked Followers cannot be sent; Deed spaces require exact types.
answers.evidence: Gunpowder Tower table

answers.answer: The unique leader gains 1 coin; the two tied last players pay nothing.
answers.evidence: Census: unique leader gains 1; tied last place pays nothing

answers.answer: After the entire 18th round including its event, before scoring, the unique player with the most built Trading Stations takes the set-aside Citizen. It counts as a collected Citizen in final scoring.
answers.evidence: Scoring: before scoring unique most takes Citizen; stations and collected Citizens score together

answers.answer: Remove the lighter Pilgrimage tile, shuffle the other 17 Hour Glass tiles face down, then place Pilgrimage on top. In Phase 1, the Start Player reveals the top tile.
answers.evidence: Setup: Hour Glass preparation; Turn Structure Phase 1

answers.answer: Each remaining coin scores 1 victory point.
answers.evidence: Scoring table: Coins — 1 each

answers.answer: Development Status starts at 1 and initial draw allowance is 4.
answers.evidence: Setup step 2

answers.answer: Only lost Development Points can be regained. Surrendered goods, Followers, Trading Stations, Place Tiles, and Technology tiles are removed from the game, not returned to supplies.
answers.evidence: Torture: items removed; “Only lost Development Points can be regained”

answers.answer: You may choose your actions’ order freely; neither printed board order nor order filled is mandated.
answers.evidence: Actions: “Choose your actions’ order freely”

answers.answer: Its passive ability is available immediately, including during the current Action Phase, as soon as acquired.
answers.evidence: Village Trader: acquired Place and passive special ability available immediately

answers.answer: You may send just one or both. Town Hall may permanently send “one or both” of its Followers in one action.
answers.evidence: Town Hall and Beneficial Deeds

answers.answer: Taking a good during Ship or Wagon movement is optional; you may complete the move and leave the available good on the connection.
answers.evidence: Movement and goods

answers.answer: Yes. You may send the two Town Hall Followers in separate action turns during the same Action Phase, before you pass; they need not both be transferred in one action.
answers.evidence: FAQ: Town Hall in separate action turns
